description:
The Education Assistance Scheme for Ph.D. candidates is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India under the aegis of the GBOCWWB, which stands for the Goa Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board.

This scheme was officially launched on January 1, 2020.

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to the children of registered construction workers who are pursuing a Ph.D. degree.

The scheme aims to encourage higher education among the children of construction workers by alleviating the financial burden associated with pursuing a doctoral degree.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is set at INR 25,000 per annum for each eligible applicant.

This amount is intended to cover various educational expenses including tuition fees, research materials, and other related costs.

The scheme specifically targets children of registered construction workers who have been working in the sector for a minimum of three years.

To be eligible for this scheme, applicants must be the biological or legally adopted children of registered construction workers.

The age limit for applicants is set at a maximum of 30 years at the time of applying for the assistance.

The educational requirement stipulates that applicants must be enrolled in a recognized university or institution for a Ph.D. program.

The scheme is applicable to all recognized universities across India.

To apply for the Education Assistance Scheme, applicants must follow a specific process.

The first step is to obtain the application form which is available on the official GBOCWWB website.

Applicants must fill out the form with accurate personal details including name, age, and educational qualifications.

Along with the application form, applicants are required to submit a copy of their admission letter from the university.

They must also provide proof of their parent’s registration as a construction worker with the GBOCWWB.

This proof can be in the form of a registration certificate issued by the board.

Additionally, applicants must submit a self-declaration stating that they are not receiving any other financial assistance for their Ph.D. studies from any other government scheme.

Once the application is complete with all necessary documents, it must be submitted to the nearest GBOCWWB office.

The application can also be submitted online through the GBOCWWB portal.

After submission, the application will be reviewed by the concerned authorities.

The review process typically takes about 30 days from the date of submission.

If the application is approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly to the bank account of the applicant.

Disbursement of funds is done on a yearly basis.

The scheme is designed to be renewable each year as long as the applicant continues to meet the eligibility criteria.

There are no specific deadlines for applying as the scheme is ongoing.

However, applicants are encouraged to apply as soon as they receive their admission to ensure timely disbursement of funds.

The GBOCWWB is the implementing authority for this scheme.

The board operates under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India.

For any queries or assistance, applicants can contact the GBOCWWB office directly.

The contact details for the GBOCWWB can be found on their official website.

The scheme has been instrumental in supporting the education of many deserving candidates.

As of the latest reports, over 500 applications have been received since the launch of the scheme.

Out of these, approximately 300 applications have been approved for financial assistance.

The scheme has a budget allocation of INR 1 crore for the financial year 2023-2024.

This allocation is expected to increase in subsequent years based on the demand and number of applicants.

The GBOCWWB is committed to ensuring that the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted periodically to assess its impact.

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme further.

The Education Assistance Scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Government of India to enhance educational opportunities for marginalized communities.

The scheme reflects the government's commitment to promoting higher education and skill development among the workforce.

It aims to create a more educated workforce that can contribute to the nation’s development.

The scheme is also aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations, particularly Goal 4 which emphasizes quality education.

In conclusion, the Education Assistance Scheme for Ph.D. candidates under the GBOCWWB is a significant step towards empowering the children of construction workers.

It provides them with the financial support necessary to pursue advanced education.

This initiative not only benefits individual families but also contributes to the overall upliftment of the construction worker community.

The scheme is a testament to the government's efforts in ensuring that education is accessible to all, regardless of their socio-economic background.
